SAILING_FOR_IMPACT.title: Regattas for Impact
SAILING_FOR_IMPACT.short: Charity regattas and sailing events that bring sailors, companies and supporters together to fund the schools.
SAILING_FOR_IMPACT.body: Regattas are where we meet the people who can make this work possible. We intend to partner with established clubs to add a charity dimension to existing races, invite sponsors and supporters on board, and one day organise a regatta of our own that carries the foundation’s name.

COASTAL_SCHOOL_RENEWAL.title: Schools in Africa
COASTAL_SCHOOL_RENEWAL.short: Renovating and equipping existing schools in African communities, starting with countries such as Morocco and Kenya.
COASTAL_SCHOOL_RENEWAL.body: We do not build parallel structures. We intend to work with existing schools, their communities, local authorities and established local partner organisations to fund well-scoped improvements: safe classrooms, clean water and sanitation, solar power, furniture, books and learning materials. Work is delivered with the required local authorisations and verified on completion.

BLUE_HORIZONS_SCHOLARSHIPS.title: Blue Horizons Scholarships
BLUE_HORIZONS_SCHOLARSHIPS.short: Modest, needs-based support so that students of our partner schools can keep learning.
BLUE_HORIZONS_SCHOLARSHIPS.body: Small awards for school fees, uniforms, books and the step to secondary or vocational education, for students of our partner schools. Awards are made through transparent criteria, with local partners and independent review, and paid directly to schools or suppliers wherever possible.

ANNUAL_GALA.title: Annual Blue Legacy Gala
ANNUAL_GALA.short: A small, elegant evening by the sea that gathers supporters and funds the schools.
ANNUAL_GALA.body: An evening of restrained elegance, timed around the regatta season, where supporters hear directly about the schools they help to fund. We will report gross and net results separately, so everyone can see what the evening truly contributes.

hero.title: From the regatta course to the classroom.
hero.lead: The Blue Legacy Foundation is being established to renovate and equip existing schools in Africa, starting with countries such as Morocco and Kenya, and to bring sailors, companies and supporters together around regattas and events that fund this work.

mission.title: Every child deserves a classroom that works.
mission.body: In many communities in Africa, children learn in crowded classrooms without clean water, light or enough books. We want to help change that, carefully and properly: one school at a time, with local partners who know the community, funded by supporters we meet on the water and at our events, and reporting exactly what we do with every euro.

hero.title: Patient, accountable philanthropy for education in Africa.
hero.lead: We intend to connect the generosity of the sailing community and its supporters with the needs of children in African schools, with the discipline of a well-run institution from the very first day.

mission.statement: Our proposed mission is to improve access to good education for children in Africa, starting with countries such as Morocco and Kenya, by renovating and equipping existing schools with local partners and supporting students’ next steps, funded transparently by a community of supporters gathered around sailing and the sea.

items.title: Stewardship
items.body: Every euro is held in trust. We plan prudently, keep a reserve, and spend on what works.

items.title: Candour
items.body: We say what is proposed, what is confirmed and what went wrong. No inflated numbers, ever.

items.title: Dignity
items.body: Children and communities are partners, not props. We never use images or stories of young people without proper consent.

items.title: Local ownership
items.body: Schools and communities decide what they need. We fund their priorities through local partners, not our own assumptions.

items.title: Restraint
items.body: Elegance without excess. Our regattas, events and administration stay proportionate to our mission.

items.title: Safety first
items.body: Safeguarding of children and safe building standards come before speed or visibility.

theory.title: From a gift to a lasting difference
theory.lead: Our working hypothesis, which we will test and revise with evidence:

steps.title: Resources
steps.body: Contributions from founding families, companies, regatta and gala supporters and individual donors, plus volunteer expertise.

steps.title: Activities
steps.body: Fund school renovations and equipment with vetted local partners and authorities; award modest scholarships; hold regattas and events to raise funds.

steps.title: Outputs
steps.body: Safer classrooms, water, sanitation, light and learning materials delivered on budget; scholarships awarded fairly; supporters engaged.

steps.title: Outcomes
steps.body: Better daily learning conditions, more regular attendance and more students continuing their education.

steps.title: Long-term impact
steps.body: Communities where a child’s education does not depend on where they were born, with a lasting network of supporters behind them.

theory.assumptions: Key assumptions we must verify: that reliable local partner organisations can be found and vetted in each country; that works can be authorised and delivered within a year; that funds can be transferred and accounted for transparently across borders; and that regattas and events raise clearly more than they cost.

methodology.title: How we will measure — and what we will not do
items: Record a baseline before any project starts, agreed with the school, the community and the local partner.
Choose a small number of indicators per project, defined in advance and published with the project.
Collect only the data we need. Data about children is aggregated and anonymised.
Release funds in instalments against verified milestones, with photos, local technical sign-off and site visits.
Publish results, including delays, overruns and things that did not work.
Never report outputs we have not delivered, nor count beneficiaries more than once.

governance.title: Built to be trusted
governance.lead: These are intentions to be formalised in the statute with Italian legal and accounting advisers. They are not yet in force.
items: A board that includes independent members, not only founding families.
A written conflicts-of-interest policy, with declarations recorded annually.
Grant decisions taken against published criteria, documented and minuted.
Local partners vetted before any grant, with written agreements and funds released in instalments.
Dual authorisation for payments and segregation of financial duties.
Annual accounts reviewed by a qualified professional, and an annual public report.
A designated safeguarding lead and a child-safeguarding policy before any activity involving children.
Sponsors and donors have no say over the selection of individual beneficiaries.

hero.title: Regattas that build schools.
hero.lead: Sailing is our community and our meeting place. We use regattas and sailing events to bring together the supporters, companies and sailors who fund education in Africa, and one day we hope to sail a regatta of our own.

items.title: Charity partner at existing regattas
items.body: We intend to partner with established clubs to add a charity dimension to races they already run: a collection, a prize-giving, a supporters’ evening.

items.title: Meeting funders on the water
items.body: Regattas gather owners, crews, sponsors and businesses. Hospitality and guest places let us introduce our school projects to the people who can support them.

items.title: Sponsors with a purpose
items.body: Companies can sponsor a race, a trophy or a crew, with recognition agreed in writing and the proceeds going to school projects.

items.title: One day, our own regatta
items.body: Our long-term ambition is a Blue Legacy Regatta: an annual event carrying the foundation’s name. It is an aspiration, not yet a plan. It would need a partner club, permits, insurance and a proven track record first.

youngguns.lead: YoungGuns is a windsurfing project owned by one of the founders of The Blue Legacy Foundation. Together we want to bring the same idea from sailing to windsurfing: the community that lives on the water supports schools in Africa.
youngguns.status: Partnership being defined: activities will be confirmed after the foundation is incorporated.

items.title: Charity windsurf events
items.body: Sessions, races and beach days organised with YoungGuns, with part of the proceeds going to school projects.

items.title: A younger community
items.body: Windsurfing brings in a new generation of riders, enthusiasts and brands who can become supporters of the foundation.

items.title: Shared sponsors
items.body: Windsurf and water-sports companies will be able to support YoungGuns and the school projects together, with recognition agreed in writing.

youngguns.disclosure: Transparency: because YoungGuns is connected to a founder, every agreement will be in writing and on market terms, approved by the board without that person’s vote, and published on the Transparency page.

hero.lead: We are seeking a small number of founding partners who share our values. Everything on this page is a proposal for discussion; nothing is a confirmed sponsorship.

principles.title: How we partner
items: No partner name or logo appears anywhere until a written agreement is signed and approved.
Partners never influence the selection of individual beneficiaries.
Recognition is proportionate and tasteful. We do not offer exclusivity over schools or young people.
We carry out due diligence on every partner, and may decline support that conflicts with our mission.
We report to partners on how their contribution was used — including when plans change.

process.title: From first conversation to agreement
steps: Enquiry — tell us about your organisation and interests.
Conversation — we share plans, budgets and governance documents.
Due diligence — on both sides, including reputational and compliance checks.
Written agreement — reviewed by legal and tax advisers once the foundation is incorporated.
Recognition — only after signature, and exactly as agreed.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains how personal data submitted through this website is processed, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003 as amended.

sections.heading: Who is responsible
body: {controller}

sections.heading: What data we collect
body: Contact and enquiry forms: your name, email address, message and, for partnership enquiries, your organisation and optionally a phone number and website.
Event interest: your name, email address, optional organisation, indicative number of guests and message.
Donations (only once enabled): the amount, currency and the email address you give our payment provider. Card details are entered on Stripe's hosted page and never reach our servers.
Security data: a keyed, irreversible hash of your IP address is used for a short time to prevent abuse. We do not store your IP address in clear.

sections.heading: Why we use it and on what legal basis
body: To answer your request and manage the relationship you ask for (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, steps at your request).
To keep the website secure and prevent spam (Art. 6(1)(f), legitimate interest).
To keep donation records required by law, once donations are enabled (Art. 6(1)(c), legal obligation).
Optional statistics, only with your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)).

sections.heading: Minors
body: This website is not directed at children and we do not knowingly collect their data through it. We never publish identifying details or images of minors without documented consent from a parent or guardian and appropriate safeguards.

sections.heading: Who receives it
body: Members of the founding team who need it to respond. Service providers acting on our instructions: hosting (Vercel), database hosting, transactional email (Resend, if enabled) and payments (Stripe, if enabled). Some providers may process data outside the EEA under appropriate safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
body: Enquiries: up to 24 months after the last contact, unless a continuing relationship requires longer.
Donation records: for the period required by Italian law (normally 10 years).
Abuse-prevention hashes: up to a few hours.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and object to processing; you may withdraw consent at any time. Use the contact form to exercise your rights. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (www.garanteprivacy.it).

sections.heading: Status of the initiative
body: The Blue Legacy Foundation is a proposed initiative and is not yet incorporated. It is not a registered Third Sector Entity (ETS), it is not an ONLUS, and it cannot issue tax-deductible receipts. Nothing on this website is an offer, a solicitation of funds, or a claim of any such status.

sections.heading: Projects, events and figures

sections.heading: No partnerships implied
body: We have no partnership, sponsorship or endorsement from any organisation, event, team or person unless it is stated on this website with their written consent. Mentions of the sailing world in general do not imply any affiliation.

sections.heading: No advice
body: Nothing on this website is legal, tax, financial or investment advice.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
body: Texts and original illustrations are the property of the founding team. Third-party photographs, where used, are credited with their licence.

sections.heading: Liability and law
body: We take care to keep information accurate but cannot guarantee it is complete or current. These terms are governed by Italian law.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.intro: We want this website to be usable by everyone. We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA.

sections.heading: What we have done
body: Semantic headings and landmarks, a skip link, full keyboard navigation with visible focus, sufficient colour contrast, text alternatives, labelled form fields with clear error messages, support for reduced-motion preferences, and layouts that work from small phones to large screens.

sections.heading: Known limitations
body: This statement is based on our own testing and automated checks; an independent audit has not yet been carried out. Documents published as PDFs may not all be fully accessible.

sections.heading: Legal framework
body: As a proposed private non-profit initiative, we are not currently subject to the accessibility obligations of Law 4/2004 ("Legge Stanca") as applied by AgID; we follow its principles voluntarily.

sections.heading: Feedback
body: If you encounter a barrier, please tell us through the contact form, describing the page and the problem. We aim to respond within ten working days.
